waypoints.title: Marquee ring buffer: swap the scrolling and pending rings only at a full rotation
waypoints.evidence: 54fdbe8: tickerText/pendingText + swapRing at the rotation's onFinished (loops: 1, restart), idle swaps immediately; lint clean; parity re-captured; witness pins; COTYPE s91. Live confirmation after re-emerge is the operator's. | 2026-10-01: former title (retitled 2026-09-30, nemik title warning): MARQUEE RING BUFFER (operator live 2026-09-22: with watch notify-send hi the scrolling text blips in and out with the popups). Cause, from templates/marquee-main.qml: rebuild() replaces root.tickerText on every notifModel onCountChanged, so the Repeater tears the Row down mid-scroll. Design (operator): double-buffered rings — the SCROLLING ring loops as long as its notifications are active; a PENDING ring collects arrivals; the swap happens at a full rotation (the NumberAnimation's loop boundary), never mid-scroll; a notification that left the model is dropped at the boundary too

waypoints.title: Marquee traversal invariant: every notification scrolls fully across at least once
waypoints.next_bounded_step: none - LIVE confirm after re-emerge is the operator's (VER-MARQUEE)
waypoints.evidence: 2bbf9c5: marquee-body.js joinItem/queueUpsert/ringNext/ringJoin; check_marquee_body 27 of 27 (5 join, 6 ring scenarios); startRun replaces the running binding; check_qml_lint.py @QMLLINT 9 of 9 (refused HEAD 1 of 9 with the fix stashed); COTYPE s98 | 2026-10-01: former title (retitled 2026-09-30, nemik title warning): MARQUEE TRAVERSAL INVARIANT (operator 2026-09-22): a notification must ALWAYS scroll offscreen -> onscreen -> offscreen at least once; never 'just appear', never vanish, never tear visually or temporally. The s91 ring fails the at-least-once half: pendingText is rebuilt from the model on every count change, so an item that arrives and expires before the next boundary never shows. Design: a QUEUE keyed by notification id (the model's IdRole / index key) — an arrival is appended with shown=false; at a boundary the next ring is [every queued item with shown=false] (expired or not), which then scrolls exactly once; an item still in the model after its rotation may be re-queued (it keeps cycling while active); an item removed from the model finishes its current rotation and is dropped at the boundary; the ring NEVER changes mid-rotation. Pure functions in marquee-body.js (ringNext(queue, modelIds) -> {ring, queue}) so the headless harness proves the invariant on synthetic arrival/expiry sequences

waypoints.title: One display engine: a pip is a segment, and only the primitive's shape differs
waypoints.rank_reason: collapse: the deepest one available — it folds the segment display and the matrix field into one engine, makes the physics layer (W33) a property of the shared emission model rather than per-surface work, and puts the matrix under the symmetry oracle that just found a defect in it

THREE layers, not two -- DISPLAY (how a primitive is drawn; means the same on every mount), MOUNT (what string exists and how it behaves; never reaches the display), INSTRUMENT (changes neither; exists so a human can see what the widget did -- debugLog/traceLog, which would have been smuggled into one of the other two if the layer were not named). ⚑ THE FINDING: the display rows are THE SAME FOUR PARAMETERS UNDER TWO VOCABULARIES. showGhost=showField (is the unlit substrate visible), ghostWeight=ghostAlpha (how subordinate), weight=dotFill (the primitive's fill fraction of its cell), digitGap=pitchScale (the lattice pitch). The LABELS diverge as far as the keys: 'Show ghost segments' vs 'Show unlit field' for one quantity. And bloom has NO marquee counterpart although the same engine draws both -- one mount can reach the emission model, the other cannot, and nothing recorded that choice. The live wallpaper declares NO config page, so its display parameters are not differently named but UNREACHABLE: three mounts, three different answers to 'can the user set the pitch'. NEXT BOUNDED STEP: make the display layer ONE declaration that each mount includes, so a new display parameter appears on every mount or is WITHHELD DELIBERATELY as a recorded act. The kcfg templates are the site (templates/clock-config.kcfg, marquee-config.kcfg, live-wallpaper-config.kcfg) and check_config_page is the gate that can already see both. ⚑ DO NOT COLLAPSE THE MOUNT ROWS: use24h is meaningless to a marquee and hoverPause to a clock -- that repetition CARRIES IDENTITY.

Root placement sidesteps it; measure before designing around it. ⚑ THE WITNESS MUST ASSERT, NEVER LIST: a claim that merely says make_gtk exists is the vacuous class the grader marks indeterminate.

waypoints.title: Let a claim cite a gate that must deny, without sitting red forever
waypoints.next_bounded_step: paperkit-e2 answered (2026-09-23): do (b), opa_gate.py --expect denied on OUR side; paperkit keeps one exit meaning (0 pass, 3 could-not-run, else fail). THE DECIDING DETAIL for their Delta grader: --expect must assert the TYPED denial — the gate ran, reached a decision, the decision is DENY, and the reason is the expected rule (e.g. --expect denied:S0) — never merely "not allow" or "non-zero". A crash/parse error/import failure must be a FAILURE (or exit 3 if the gate genuinely could not run); otherwise every mutation that breaks the reader passes and the claim grades vacuous. Build after the W50 batch-2 agent lands (both touch opa_gate.py). Then cite: refuses noise-only.log (S0), and a colour-only fixture (U1).
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-01: former title (retitled 2026-09-30, nemik title warning): A CLAIM THAT A GATE MUST DENY: paperkit reads exit 1 as an open item, so a negative fixture (serial noise-only.log -> DENY S0; a colour-only painter -> DENY U1; a torn-read writer -> DENY) cannot be cited without sitting red forever. Proposal from the serial-claims agent: an inverting check type in catalog/worklist/paper.toml ([checks.refuses]: passes only when the cited gate exits 1), or "opa_gate.py --expect denied". Then a claim fails in BOTH directions: if the reader starts admitting noise, or if it cannot read the file at all. Touches paperkit check-type surface: ask paperkit whether [checks.X] may invert, before building.

Under the NumberAnimation the item-11 run ended before 5600. So a run takes longer in the harness VIRTUAL time: the harness clock is a NumberAnimation on the fixed-step animation driver, while FrameAnimation ticks per RENDERED frame, and the offscreen platform renders fewer frames per virtual second than a display vsync. | 2026-10-01: 2026-10-01 MEASURED from the saved trace samples (40 ms virtual): the harness runs at 60 frames per virtual second (33.3 px per 32 ms = 2 frames, 49.9 px per 48 ms = 3; one frame = 4.618 pips x 3.6 px/pip = 16.6 px) - the "fewer frames" hypothesis is FALSIFIED. Runs are FASTER than before (~0.6 s vs the old 1.5 s duration floor). L2 is a PHASE coincidence: flash cycles to 5100, silent runs 5120-5700, id 2 arrives 5200 mid-run, is replaced 5600, next swap 5728 shows "second - changed"; the old 1.5 s floor happened to swap near 5420, inside the 400 ms arrival-to-replace window. waypoints.title: Marquee replace: changed characters roll vertically (old out, new in) while the run keeps panning horizontally
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-01: 2026-10-01 OPERATOR DECISION (W178): a replace is shown as a vertical roll of the changed characters - removed ones rotate out, added ones rotate in - while the whole notification keeps panning horizontally; at a 10 Hz replace rate the changing piece is seen rolling as it pans. | 2026-10-01: 2026-10-01 DESIGN (W183, operator decision + defaults stated to operator, unopposed): RENDER MODEL read from templates/marquee-main.qml 417-599: text is painted into ApertureField backdrop at scale=4 px per pip, rows from the registry (5x8 => 8 rows), each glyph cell at rep.offs[i]; the field grades brightness from the backdrop under each aperture. So a vertical offset in BACKDROP px is a graded sub-pip roll by construction (4 sub-steps per pip; the same fractional motion S8 wants horizontally). DECISIONS: (a) changed span = common prefix/suffix diff of the item text, rolled per glyph cell; (b) odometer direction: old moves up and out, new rises from below, travel = (rows+1) cells so the two glyphs never touch; (c) length change: cells past the shorter text roll from/to blank, and the suffix GLIDES horizontally by the width delta on the same progress (offs interpolated), so nothing jumps - the W45 never-tear invariant; (d) a replace of an item NOT on the ring stays a queue upsert (L2 judges by id); (e) cost: drawBackdrop runs per frame only while a roll is live. | 2026-10-01: 2026-10-01 OPERATOR RULINGS on the design review: (1) the vertical roll REPLACES L3 for an on-board replace - L3 cannot hold for a replace before the first frame (a race); W189 retires L3 for replaces and judges the roll. (2) cells inside the span whose old and new glyph are identical hold still (no self-roll flicker) - agreed. (3) on board = the span current position: not yet entered -> apply; on the board -> roll; scrolled past -> apply and W185 queues a second pass. (4) WIDTH CHANGE: no segment ever outruns the pan; segments only STALL - a shortened replace (ABBC->ABC) stalls the LEADING segment until the shortened follower catches up; a lengthened one (AABCC->AABBCC) stalls the TRAILING segment while the lengthened leader folds in. Replaces the earlier suffix-glide default. Stated defaults: reduced motion swaps instantly; job progress keeps its gauge path; bold/link/critical styling carried through the roll; roll continues under hover-pause; repaint only span cells. | 2026-10-13: W183 closed 2026-10-13 on its own stated test (done when W186 to W189 land), re-read from the cards: W186 replaceSpan done 20261002, W187 FrameAnimation port done 20261001, W188 paint the roll done 20261002, W189 live L-rule done 20261003. The one uncovered case the children name (a SHORTENED replace is held by the body harness M12 and M13, not by a live case) is W242.

waypoints.title: S8 refuses an animation with under 2/3 of its moving steps fractional; zero steps excluded, all-stall withheld
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-01: 2026-10-01 from W203 --frames: high-mismatch whole readings are a measurement artifact; S8 must not count them as whole. | 2026-10-13: W201 landed 2026-10-13: policy/screens.rego S8 refuses an animation with under 2/3 of its MOVING steps fractional (whole = within 0.001 of an integer), reading the harness logged offsets where present (exact) else the image fit; zero steps excluded; a run with no step or only stalls is withheld and not admitted. waypoints.title: The scroll fit models a sub-pip move as linear blending, but the aperture field grades by coverage; fix the model, not the grid
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-01: 2026-10-01 MEASURED with check_screens --frames on the W200 attempt-2 render (marquee-anim-EL-Amber, 36 pairs): ONE run frames 1-35 (total brightness rises, flat 6.89 frames 13-22, falls), every shift forward +4.0..+5.0; frame 18 shift +4.375 mismatch 3.71 of 6.89 (54% > 50% tolerance) = the S5 TEAR; frame 13 mismatch 3.44 (50%). Mismatch cycles 0.02 / 1.26 / 1.85 / 0.02 / 3.7 with the step phase. NOT a restart: a measurement artifact - the step falls between the fit grid points. Same cause as the W201 whole-pip under-read. | 2026-10-02: 2026-10-01 PREMISE FALSIFIED BY ARITHMETIC before any code: FRACTIONS = i/8 (render_screens:502) includes 0.625, 0.007 pip from the true 0.618 - a grid error that small cannot produce a 54% mismatch. The fitted shifts for a CONSTANT 4.618-pip step read 4.0..5.0, so the fit picks wrong k/f when model error dominates. Cause: best_pip_shift models brightness after a sub-pip move as LINEAR interpolation between neighbouring pips (cur[c] ~ (1-f) prev[c+k] + f prev[c+k+1]); the ApertureField grades each pip by coverage under round apertures (dotFill 0.82, gamma) - nonlinear, phase-dependent misfit. | 2026-10-02: 2026-10-02 CLOSED on its own condition (done when W208 and W209 land): W208 put the harness own per-frame offsets into the marquee APNG; W209 made S5 judge logged animations by those offsets (a step off the run constant step is a tear; no fit, no tolerance), keeping the linear-blend fit only where no log exists. The model defect this waypoint named (linear blending vs coverage-graded aperture) no longer decides any verdict on a logged animation - it is bypassed by measuring what the harness did. W200 (the frame-18 marquee tear) and W201 are unblocked.

waypoints.title: Cursor ghost layer: decide whether glyphs carry the ghost token (the unlit-segment idiom) and draw it if so
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-02: Split from W36 (2026-10-02); the ghost layer was listed as optional in W36 next step. | 2026-10-03: 2026-10-03 (swarm): DECIDED BY MEASUREMENT (the card suggested operator samples; the agent measured instead - overrule with a --sheet render if wanted): glyphs carry the ghost token exactly where a frame leaves a segment unlit, drawn as the palette ghost at its solved ghost_alpha; a static glyph has no unlit segment so carries no ghost. Each wait frame shows lit ink ~35 px and ghost ink 21-24 px at 32 px; a planted magenta ghost drops the ghost ink to 0-2 px, so the measurement can see a wrong ghost. Policy C11 requires lit and ghost ink in every frame of an animated shape. Weakness stated: the ghost-ink count is a pixel match with tolerance 3 per channel (antialiased edges can match by chance); separation 21-24 vs 0-2 is large.

waypoints.title: Palette solver as a nodal solve: drive make_palette from the palette_relations netlist through gcalc.solver, searching only the residual discrete choice
waypoints.next_bounded_step: On the W227 ruling: core -> make_palette reads gcalc.solver for the linear relations (ghost divider first, then lightness/signed contrast), with N3 as the regression guard; sibling -> close W221 on the witness shape (check_nodal + policy/nodal N2/N3), its separation and ghost-floor work carried by W226 and W228.
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-02: 2026-10-02 operator asked whether the solver uses the g-calculus conductance / nodal approach. Measured: NO. palette_relations.py states the constraints as a gcalc.solver netlist (from palette_graph edges; terminals view/fg/fg_act; ghost as lit-ghost-ground divider verified with gcalc.solver.laplacian) and netlist_render + check_relations + check_palette_graph run it, but make_palette imports neither palette_relations nor gcalc: it searches (~40 candidates/slot, max-min hill-climb, seeded restarts) and the ghost uses ghost_solve closed form, which palette_relations calls a re-derivation defect. palette_relations.open_questions L151-156: nodal is continuous, occupancy discrete; Voronoi/Delaunay over candidates proposed, unmeasured; no Voronoi/Delaunay code exists. | 2026-10-02: 2026-10-02 CORRECTION (operator: "oh bull. That just means you have more linear channels to solve, and those channels constrain each other"): the earlier evidence that slot occupancy and sector hue are inherently discrete was wrong - occupancy is discrete only because the search enumerates ~40 candidates; a sector is a convex cone in the a/b plane; contrast is linear in Y once its sign is a variable; CVD views are linear maps. palette_relations.open_questions L151 makes the same mistaken split and needs the same correction when W221 lands. | 2026-10-02: 2026-10-02 SEPARATION RE-READ (operator: "See how g-calculus achieves NOT()"): gcalc NOT = the reciprocal x -> 1/x, conductance <-> resistance (kernel.py:3-9, NOT = lambda x: 1/x; exact.py:103 G_NOT = swap of the (n,d) halves, det -1); OR = parallel (add), AND = series ab/(a+b) = Kron/Schur reduction of a degree-2 node (laws.py:293-300); De Morgan from the involution alone; sign is a parity bit, never a negative value (symbolic.py:56, 238). So "apart" = NOT(near) = resistance between the two slot nodes, a lower bound on gcalc.solver.r_eff - a positive-cone quantity, not the exclusion of a ball. The ball is the coordinate picture; it vanishes when separation is read as a resistance between nodes. Open: measure that a lower bound on r_eff behaves as a usable constraint in this solve (effective conductance = min energy over potentials), not asserted. | 2026-10-02: 2026-10-02 STEP 1 DONE (gcalc.solver read): netlist(pairs) -> Layered of (u,v) -> admittance term (Q pairs, nothing divided until evaluate); laplacian(nodes, edges, env) evaluates each term with env and builds an exact Fraction Laplacian; r_eff(nodes, edges, env, s, t) solves the reduced system; frontier_solve/freeze/step do symbolic star-mesh elimination (order = gauge, Q count = cost, verdict halt/stop). In el-openglo gcalc is used SYMBOLICALLY only (netlist_render frames/cycle_edges, check_relations): no env has ever been bound to measured palette values - the numeric solve does not exist yet. ORIENTATION QUESTION (hypothesis-is-ambiguity): palette_relations says y >= 1 clears, i.e. admittance = margin ratio (separated = HIGH conductance), while the NOT reading says apart = 1/near (separated = HIGH resistance). The two are each other under G_NOT; the model does not say which is the conductance, so step 2 measures both. | 2026-10-02: 2026-10-02 STEP 2 RAN - FIRST NUMERIC NODAL SOLVE: scripts/check_nodal.py --json (margin per colour edge, bound as resistance = conductance 1/m, gcalc NOT; gcalc.solver.r_eff over each component) + policy/nodal.rego (N0 empty/unsolved, N1 clears-alone-but-r_eff<1) + nodal_test.rego (15/15 with lib); selftest passes (lone edge r_eff == margin; near chain seen; Rayleigh holds; components solved apart). RESULT: opa_gate nodal DENIED 177 of 192 edges, 15 admitted, 18 withheld (ghost ceiling/floor and the APCA argmax have no margin form). blocked_on: operator: decide how much halo wash the clock default may have. Measured on EL-Openglo, the share of the face off the ground colour is 18.8 percent with no bloom, 40.7 at bloom 1, 48.6 at 2, 54.0 at 3, 55.4 at the default 4, 42.7 at 6; the digits stay legible at all of them (contact sheet sent). Options: A keep the default bloom 4 and gate only legibility (stroke against halo contrast), B lower the default to about 1.5 (about 45 percent wash) and cap the halo radius at a few stroke widths, C leave as is and close the card as resolved by the earlier fixes
waypoints.next_bounded_step: Operator decision pending (see blocked_on); on a ruling, bound the halo in stroke widths and gate the wash fraction in rego
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-03: Operator report 2026-10-03 (screenshot: EL Segment Clock Settings with lit weight high, unlit weight 0, pitch low, bloom ~65%; the panel clock shows near-88:88 blobs; "I bet tesseract would say 88:88"). MEASURED in the render harness (render_qml clock 160x48, RHI/llvmpipe, EL-Openglo): config DOES reach the pixels there (showGhost=false drops ghost-ish 206 -> 6; bloom 0/1/2.5/4 gives other-pixels 762/3559/5439/5960 of 7680, ground 6072/3174/1432/994). So the harness does not reproduce "ignores"; it reproduces the UNREADABLE face: the halo is blurMax = round(strokeLit*2*bloom) px (SegmentChar.qml L127), ~24 px at the default bloom 4.0 on a 48 px panel, i.e. half the digit height, and the modal colour of the whole face moves from ground #0c1f1a to #142c26. Past ~2.5 the wash saturates, so moving the dialog slider between 65% and 100% changes nothing visible, which can read as the dialog being ignored. NOT verified: that the real Plasma applet receives the dialog values (no Plasma runtime here; check_config_page proves only that each kcfg entry declares value+default and each mount names its key). tesseract is installed (/usr/bin/tesseract) but read nothing from the raw render (no inversion/scale), so no OCR verdict yet. | 2026-10-03: Operator follow-ups 2026-10-03: (1) even without bloom the face is near-unreadable and the unlit stroke weight is nonresponsive; (2) ghost brightness too high and not adjustable. MEASURED: Segment snaps every stroke to an even integer >= 2 px (SegmentChar t = 2*max(1,round(thick/2))) and segThick floors at 2 at 48 px, so lit (2.5 -> 2 px) and unlit (0.4*2 = 0.8 -> 2 px) are the SAME stroke and the lit/unlit distinction is opacity alone (palette-solved ghost alpha 0.566, high); the unlit slider floor was 0.3, inside the dead zone. SHIPPED: unlit weight 0 = no ghost (slider floor now 0); clock exposes Unlit opacity (default the solved alpha, 0-1; verified 0.05 vs 0.9 differ on screen; baked literal kept as ghostAlpha, override in cfgGhostAlpha). NOT FIXED: the stroke quantisation (W265, operator-visible restyle) and the high DEFAULT ghost alpha (a palette-solved relation: re-solving it is a W-level change, not a dialog fix). Mistake of mine: my first version replaced the baked alpha literal and check_ghost_surfaces refused 6 of 6 clock variants while the commit still passed (cotype is non-blocking): fixed next commit, gate gap minted as W266. | 2026-10-12: 2026-10-12 wash measured (clock 160x48, pixels farther than 12 per channel from the ground; bloom 0 is the strokes and ghost alone). EL-Openglo: bloom 0 18.8 pct, 1 40.7, 2 48.6, 3 54.0, 4 55.4 (the default), 6 42.7 (a larger blur thins below the tolerance). EL-Amber-Lit: 18.8, 38.0, 44.1, 48.5, 48.4, 32.2. The wash saturates by bloom 2 to 3. A contact sheet (bloom 0 to 6, EL-Openglo) shows the digits stay clearly legible at every value, including the default 4, with a soft green wash on the ground; the original unreadable report combined lit weight high, unlit weight 0 and pitch low, and the stroke snapping and ghost settings were fixed since. So the default is legible and the open question is taste: how much ground wash is acceptable

waypoints.title: Converge SegmentChar and ApertureField toward one display component with swappable geometry (one renderer for every surface)
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-12: 2026-10-12 INVENTORY (SegmentChar.qml read whole, ApertureField.qml read). MECHANICS BOTH IMPLEMENT: (1) a GHOST pass of unlit primitives: colour, alpha (ghostAlpha, glow), show flag; SegmentChar draws the unlit segments, the field every pip as a floor. (2) a LIT pass at a coverage: SegmentChar lit segments at coverage 1 times glow, the field a pip at the aperture coverage; (3) the EMISSION HALO, already shared (W500, W501: EmissionHalo, bloom, haloOpacity, glow, radiusUnit); (4) one brightness relation: perceived brightness is luminance times AREA (SegmentChar: stroke weight and coverage thick over t; field: ghostOpacity + coverage times (1 - ghostOpacity), then the gamma curve); (5) a glow multiplier on the whole cell; (6) a mount-owned layout (segLen, cellGap, colon; pitch, rows, y0). GEOMETRY-SPECIFIC, the one swappable input: SegmentChar: the substrate tables (segGeom, digSegs), device-grid snapped rounded bars, ghostWeight stroke thickness, the lit gradient and boundary depth along a bar, the weight between grid widths (litExtra underlay), the colon; ApertureField: the pip grid, dotFill, the backdrop canvas and its prefix-sum aperture integral, scrolling offset, colour from ink, the ring. SHARED INTERFACE PROPOSED: a primitive set with per-primitive coverage in 0 to 1 (a segment is a bar at coverage 0 or 1, a pip a dot at the aperture coverage) feeding three layers in this order, ghost then halo then crisp lit, with emission (litColor, ghostColor, ghostAlpha, showGhost, glow, bloom, haloOpacity) as the common properties. The display_params rows already encode the split: Withheld geometry rows (litWeight, ghostWeight, litGradient, boundaryDepth on the field; apertureGamma, backdropScale on the strokes) are exactly the geometry-specific values. STEP ORDER, each holding stills, parity baselines and the reach witness: ghost layer, then the primitive coverage interface, then the lit layer and the brightness relation | 2026-10-13: All three children landed: W532 ghost layer (6dd3922), W533 Primitive (8a8cc19), W534 lit layer and brightness relation. SegmentChar and ApertureField now share Primitive, GhostLayer, LitLayer and EmissionHalo; the geometry (segment tables and snapping; pip grid, backdrop and aperture integral) is the one swappable input. Follow-up W537 (reach arm for the lit core).

waypoints.title: el-openglo commit gate is red: pre-commit selftests fail and the @EBUILD check's git write-tree exits 128
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-06: 2026-10-06 ROOT CAUSE of the seven failing selftests (reproduced): under a partial commit git exports GIT_INDEX_FILE (relative .git/next-index-N.lock) and GIT_DIR into the hook; a selftest that builds a throwaway repo (git -C tmp init, add .) inherits it, stages into the wrong index file, and reads an empty population (check_emitters_run fails with the variable set, passes plain; verified with GIT_INDEX_FILE=.git/next-index-kata.lock). FIX: .githooks/pre-commit runs each selftest through env -u GIT_INDEX_FILE -u GIT_DIR -u GIT_WORK_TREE -u GIT_PREFIX; the gates keep the environment. A first attempt (scrubbing GIT_* in check_emitters_run.run_in) did not fix it and was reverted. NOT yet verified end to end: the whole hook is being run under the simulated commit environment. The @EBUILD git write-tree exit 128 is not explained by this. | 2026-10-06: 2026-10-06 VERIFIED: bash .githooks/pre-commit under GIT_INDEX_FILE=.git/next-index-kata.lock exits 0, 'all gates pass' (the cotype queue arm FAILs but is non-blocking: open @RESIDUE). The @EBUILD git write-tree exit 128 was the same inherited-environment cause, not index-lock contention. Commit of .githooks/pre-commit and the queue started. | 2026-10-06: 2026-10-06 CORRECTION to the entry above, measured on a throwaway repo (scratchpad/partial_commit_probe.py): in a partial commit the hook gets an ABSOLUTE GIT_INDEX_FILE=.git/next-index-N.lock and git write-tree WORKS with it (rc 0), but with the GIT_* variables removed it exits 128 because the commit holds the real index locked. So (1) the seven fixture selftests failed because they inherited GIT_INDEX_FILE (fixed: each selftest runs with GIT_* removed, which my first real commit showed works), but (2) check_ebuild must KEEP the commit's environment: its selftest needs it, and the @EBUILD gate loses it because paperkit's check sandbox is default-deny (paperkit/checkenv.py clean_env keeps only an allow-list plus LC_ and PAPERKIT_ prefixes). FIX 2: the hook exports PAPERKIT_GIT_INDEX_FILE, check_ebuild.staged_tree restores GIT_INDEX_FILE from it for its one write-tree call, and check_ebuild's selftest is exempt from the scrub. The earlier simulated probe passed because it did not hold the index lock; the probe now does. Second real commit started. Upstream fix: summit ask-project-declared-env-passthrough (open, filed by paperkit for el-openglo). | 2026-10-06: 2026-10-06 commit 2a4f9b8 landed through el-openglo's real pre-commit gate: the hook fix (selftests without the commit's GIT_*, the commit's index passed to @EBUILD as PAPERKIT_GIT_INDEX_FILE). Root causes measured on a throwaway repo, scratchpad/partial_commit_probe.py

waypoints.title: The marquee falls back to ? for characters outside the registry font: wire arbitrary glyphs (Unifont via the viewport) so the board absorbs them
waypoints.next_bounded_step: Umbrella: work W512 first (the rasteriser rule, parity-checked on registry glyphs), then W513, then W514; the painter then falls back to the memoised raster instead of the question mark
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-12: Operator 2026-10-12: the matrix font is not meant to be uppercase and digits only; it should absorb more arbitrary glyphs. Existing pieces: W47 (done, folded into W54) gave ApertureField backdropRows and offsetY and read Unifont 1:1 through a 16-row backdrop; W30 is the font compiler; W26 authored the 5x8 descender table. The painter still takes only registry glyphs via Body.glyphFor, whose last fallback is the question mark | 2026-10-12: Operator 2026-10-12: the registry lacks almost the whole Unicode set, so measuring the missing set is moot. Design: render on demand and memoise, with pre-rendering from system locale settings. Atomized into W512 (one rasteriser rule), W513 (memo cache), W514 (locale prewarm). Risk: an on-demand Canvas render runs on the GUI thread, which W510 shows already saturated, so the memo must make a miss a one-time cost

waypoints.title: One glyph rasteriser rule shared by Python and QML: a font glyph becomes 5x8 (or 8x16) column bytes by one threshold rule, parity-checked on the registry glyphs
Memoise rendered glyphs on demand: key (codepoint, font, cell size, rule version), miss renders once, the table persists across plasmashell restarts
waypoints.next_bounded_step: Decide in-process time-sliced versus helper process by measuring one page render cost under the Canvas route (after W512 fixes the rule), then implement the miss-first-then-page queue with the budget
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-12: Operator suggestion 2026-10-12: render the missed glyph first so its paint unblocks, then the whole page it belongs to, since one pulled glyph predicts more. Analysis: sound (demand paging with readahead). Page = an aligned Unicode block of 256 code points, clipped to what the font covers, so a CJK block costs one page not twenty thousand glyphs. The miss renders synchronously and alone, the rest of its page in a queue time-sliced to a per-frame budget so no frame is blocked, pages deduplicated while in flight, a cap on queued pages, and the page persisted as one unit. Open choice: render in the GUI thread time-sliced, or in a helper process (Python and FreeType) that writes the table the widget loads, which is the only truly off-path option. W510 says the GUI thread has no slack, which favours the helper

waypoints.title: Bisect the pummel soak CPU: vary one input at a time (critical flash, replace, job gauge, long body, item count) in the Pod and name the costly path in the marquee
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-12: Tooling: marquee_soak --mix a,b|none switches inputs (low, critical, replace, flash, job, actions, long) and soak_bisect.py runs baseline, each alone, and all in sequential Pods (100 s each), printing one row per run; selftests pass. Bisect running 2026-10-12 | 2026-10-12: Bisect 2026-10-12, 9 Pods of 100 s on the 1-core Pod: CPU percent baseline 78.1, low 78.6, critical 77.7, replace 81.0, flash 78.4, job 73.5, actions 82.2, long 76.1, all 80.8. Every row is within noise of the baseline, so NO notification input drives the cost: the baseline (one normal short item per burst) already uses about 78 pct of a core. Memory differs only for long (rss 209 to 241 MB vs 151) and all (194 to 199). Reading: the cost is intrinsic to the running board, most likely the per-frame ApertureField work (integrate() lookups plus every pip delegate cov, opacity and colour bindings re-evaluating on each new coverage array, about 1064 pips x 3 rectangles), uncapped offscreen | 2026-10-12: Result 2026-10-12, 60 s Pod runs with frames counted (Window.frameSwapped now in the harness RESULT). Idle board 1.7 pct CPU: the cost is in scrolling, and no notification input changes it. Settings: ghost off 80 pct, bigger pitch (about 20 pct fewer pips) 75, slower scroll 86 versus baseline 79. Baseline: 3684 frames, 70.5 CPU s, 19.1 ms per frame, about 44 fps; at 60 fps on the desktop that is over one core, matching the live 90 pct GUI thread. Patched staged copies: no coverage recompute on scroll (E1) 26 frames and 8.2 CPU s, so the scene stops changing; no pips (E2) 21.8 CPU s, so the JS coverage code is about a third of the cost and the pip delegates plus render the rest; colourFromInk off (E3) same 3684 frames but 44.7 CPU s, 12.1 ms per frame, a 37 pct saving. So the main costs are, in order: per-pip bindings re-evaluating when coverage and inkColour arrays are reassigned every frame, the per-frame inkColour array of Qt.rgba values, and integrate() itself

waypoints.title: Stop recomputing the per-pip ink colour on every frame: colour is a property of the painted run, so cache it per backdrop paint (E3 saves 37 percent CPU)
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-12: templates/ApertureField.qml integrate(): the three colour sums run only for a pip with ink (sum above 0), same arithmetic and order so the colour is bit-identical. Soak 60 s, 3683 frames: 17.86 ms CPU per frame versus 19.13 before, only 6.6 pct: the arithmetic on dark pips was not the main cost, the delegate bindings were (see W522)

waypoints.title: Update only the pips whose coverage changed instead of reassigning the whole coverage array, so unchanged delegates re-evaluate nothing
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-12: templates/ApertureField.qml: pip delegates hold cov and ink as plain properties and integrate() writes only those that differ (Repeater id pips, itemAt); coverage and inkColour stay assigned for whole-array readers. Soak 60 s Pod, 3684 frames: 14.66 ms CPU per frame versus 19.13 before (23 pct), total 54.0 CPU s versus 70.5; screens pixel-identical (render_screens left catalog/library unchanged); qml_lint and marquee_live admit. Remaining cost per frame: the integrate arithmetic, the itemAt sweep, lit-pip writes and the software render. Colour-from-ink off measured 12.1 ms per frame as the floor for the colour table

waypoints.title: Cut the ApertureField per-frame cost further: skip the itemAt sweep over unchanged columns, and measure integrate() against the lit-pip write and render share
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-12: Split of the 54.0 CPU s per 60 s soak after W522 (patched staged copies): floor with no integrate 8.2; integrate only 18.0 (so integrate about 9.8, 18 pct); itemAt sweep with reads and no writes 19.6 (sweep about 1.6, 3 pct); pip writes plus software render about 34.4 (64 pct, mostly the offscreen software raster the GL desktop puts on the render thread). Next cut that is exact: skip blank columns in integrate() with a per-column ink prefix (Float64) since non-negative alphas make a zero total mean every pip sum is zero | 2026-10-12: templates/ApertureField.qml: sample() builds a Float64 per-column ink prefix (colPrefix) and integrate() skips a column whose aperture range holds no ink, filling the exact zeros the row loop would. Soak 60 s Pod, 3684 frames: 13.98 ms CPU per frame, 51.5 CPU s, versus 14.66 and 54.0 after W522 and 19.13 and 70.5 originally (27 pct total). Screens pixel-identical, qml_lint, render_constants and marquee_live admit. What remains is mostly the pip writes plus the offscreen software raster (about 34 CPU s of 54 before this cut), which the GL desktop moves off the GUI thread and which this offscreen soak cannot separate

waypoints.title: Explain why the marquee measurements differ on the RHI: kerning K1 (bold interior run of 7 columns under CVD) and urgency V9 (hover-pause not measured) deny there and admit on software
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-12: 2026-10-12 kerning measurement, software versus RHI (check_kerning --json EL-Openglo, EL_MARQUEE_RHI=1 for the RHI): the RHI case lists 10 runs where software lists 9 (an extra trailing run of 3 or 4 columns, a partial glyph at the right edge), and its first bold run is 7 columns where every software bold run is 6. So the two backends capture the board at a different scroll offset or width, or antialias the pip edge differently; not a glyph-width change in the template. K1 reads the interior run, so the 7 is what denies. Urgency V9 (pausability not measured) is the other difference, still unread | 2026-10-12: 2026-10-12 CAUSE FOUND. The kerning and urgency stills use harness grab, taken at the first sample with the text mid-board: a MOMENT, so the scroll offset depends on frame timing. The same RHI run gave three different run lists at one speed. The stepped capture (frames mode, R9) is deterministic: x falls 16.55 px per frame, and software and RHI give IDENTICAL run lists frame by frame (regular and bold, frames 6, 10, 14, 18). So the RHI renders the pips the same; the K1 difference was capture phase, a latent flake on BOTH backends. Gating the stepped capture is not possible yet: at frame 14 both backends deny K1 (7-column bold run under deuteranomaly, protanomaly and tritanomaly), a real defect minted as W526. Tooling: check_kerning --json --frame N takes the stills from the stepped capture; bold_facts gained still_frame; run() gained config_overrides. Gate default unchanged and admitting. Urgency V9 on the RHI (hover pause not measured) is still unread | 2026-10-12: Both RHI differences explained. K1: the moment-grab phase (W526 holds the real defect behind it). V9: the hover-pause needs the offscreen pointer resting at (0,0), which a Wayland compositor does not have, so hovered runs now stay on the software scene graph (uses_rhi); urgency_cues admits on the RHI. RHI state now: marquee_live admit, symmetry admit, urgency_cues admit, kerning denies on the default grab until W526

waypoints.title: Bold letters bleed at some sub-pip scroll phases: K1 denies a 7-column bold run under every colour-vision view at stepped frame 14, on both scene graphs
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-12: 2026-10-12 K1 across scroll phases, software scene graph, stepped capture frames 8 to 40, widest interior lit run per view (scratch kern_phases.py: one frames run per style). Frames 8 to 22 (text fully on the board): gray view bold runs 5 or 6 at EVERY phase; the three colour-vision views reach 7 at frames 14, 17, 19 and 22 and 5 or 6 elsewhere. So the 7 is CVD-specific and phase-specific: the binarisation is to each stills OWN peak, and under the CVD channel mixing the faint half-covered neighbour pip that the bold grow (s/2) spreads onto at a sub-pip phase clears the lit threshold. A graded pip is not a bleed in the LED-board sense. Frames from 23 on show runs of 18, 30, 45 columns, also in REGULAR text under CVD views (frames 18, 23, 26, 31, 34, 39): a measurement artifact not yet explained (text leaving the board edge, or the binarisation collapsing when the peak is small) | 2026-10-12: Settled: W527 landed the phase-swept K4 (stroke-group width, stable across views, phases and scene graphs), W529 retired K1 and its guards, W528 showed the apparent garble was the still readers median baseline. Kerning is judged at every phase from frame 8 to 40 and holds

waypoints.title: Make K1 phase-robust: judge the gap column brightness against the stroke (graded, not binarised to the stills own peak) over the stepped frames of one full phase cycle, and explain the 18 to 45 column runs past frame 22
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-12: 2026-10-12 the 18 to 45 column runs explained (kept frames, lit column profiles at frames 17 to 19). At frame 18 (x=138.6) the pip image is a half-pip phase: every glyph column is split across two pips, no pip is fully lit, the gray view binarises to the stills own peak and keeps only faint scattered columns, while the colour-vision views (a different peak and threshold) keep nearly every pip and fuse the text into 18, 30 and 45 column runs. Frames 17 and 19 (aligned) give identical, clean profiles in both views. So the runs are not a defect in the board, they are the binarisation applied to a uniformly half-covered still: a binary lit-run measure is phase-fragile by construction. That settles the measure: K1 needs a graded fact, the brightness of the gap pip next to a stroke pip, judged per letter boundary at the known 6-pip advance | 2026-10-12: 2026-10-12 graded measures tried on stepped frames 8 to 24 (scratch kern_graded.py). (a) Valley ratio (gap pip over the lower neighbouring stroke): regular text 0.0 at aligned phases and up to 0.66 gray / 0.78 CVD at others; bold up to 0.91 in the CVD views, 0.66 gray; a fused pair has NO valley, so the valley alone cannot catch it (it scores 0). (b) Stroke-group width (columns at or above 0.6 of the stills peak, interior groups): regular 4 or 5, bold 5 or 6, IDENTICAL in all four views, at every phase from frame 8 to 22; a fused pair blows it out. So the stable graded fact is the stroke-group width, and the valley ratio is secondary. Frames 23, 24 and 26 show an 18-column group for BOLD in the views (frame 23 in all four): a real garbled render, unchanged with the template before W521 (8bc17e4) and with the W523 skip disabled, so not mine: minted as the bold garble card. Built in the tree and NOT yet committed: valley_ratios and gap_facts in check_urgency_cues, a measure that returns gaps in check_kerning (staged only in scratch ck.py, not installed) | 2026-10-12: 2026-10-12 landed in the tree: check_urgency_cues.stroke_groups, valley_ratios and gap_facts; check_kerning measure now returns gaps (widest interior stroke group per view and style over stepped frames 8 to 22, plus the valley ratio); policy/kerning.rego gains K4 (group wider than glyph plus bloom at some phase), K5 (cases without a sweep), K6 (fewer than 6 frames) with refusing and admitting tests, 1205 of 1205 rego tests pass. Kerning admits on software AND on the RHI. K1 still reads the moment-grab still, so on the RHI it can pass or fail by phase luck (it denied once, then admitted): its retirement in favour of K4 is the next card

waypoints.title: Bold marquee text garbles at some scroll phases: stepped frames 23, 24 and 26 show an 18-column fused stroke group in every view, with the template before and after W521 to W523 alike
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-12: 2026-10-12 characterised. (1) The widget paints every cell (trace: bold 745 cells, ink 46328 landed, regular ink equals its expected 22784), so the backdrop is sound. (2) DETERMINISTIC: three identical bold runs give pixel-identical frames 20 to 28, on software and on the RHI separately (digests differ between the two scene graphs, structure does not). So not a capture race and not a scene graph: the widget logic. (3) Frame 22 is clean text; frame 23 (offset 22 steps of 4.618 pips) is a double exposure: the text plus a dimmer wider copy at a different offset, and a uniform dim fill (about 0.09 of ink) across pips that should be empty, which the gray view normalises against a lower peak (0.20 against 0.33). (4) Not mine: identical with the ApertureField of 8bc17e4 (before W521 to W523). Regular text is clean at the same frames; bold only, from frame 23 | 2026-10-12: ROOT CAUSE: a measurement artifact, not a widget defect. check_urgency_cues.ink_views took a cell ink as |brightness - median brightness|, which is the unlit level only while most cells are unlit; bold text covers over half the board from stepped frame 23 (529 of 840 pips with coverage), the median landed on the lit level and the whole picture inverted (the double exposure and the uniform dim fill). Evidence: widget trace shows every cell lands and the coverage the board computes is sound at every offset (max 1.0, plausible lit counts); stills are pixel-identical run to run on both scene graphs; with the baseline changed to a low percentile of cell brightness (dark_baseline) the stroke groups for frames 8 to 40 are regular 4 or 5, bold 5 or 6, identical in all four views, no 18 to 45 column runs. Fix: dark_baseline in check_urgency_cues plus a kerning selftest arm for a mostly lit board; the kerning sweep widened from frames 8 to 22 to 8 to 40. kerning and urgency_cues admit; both selftests pass

waypoints.title: Retire kerning K1 (binary lit-run on a moment-grab still) in favour of the phase-swept K4, keeping the K2 and K3 population guards, with the reason recorded in the policy

waypoints.title: Marquee queues replaces that arrive during a live roll and exposes the queued count, so the roll can see the pileup
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-13: W546 measured 2026-10-13 (scratch probe, one arrival then five replace_visible of the same id 100 ms apart, live widget, EL-Openglo): replaces land at 2000, 2128, 2208, 2320, 2400 ms and the roll progress resets to 0 at each (peaks 0.12, 0.12, 0.04); nothing past 0.12 during the burst; only after the last replace does a roll run to completion (0 to 0.92 over 2400 to 2800 ms). Cause read in marquee-main.qml startRoll: rollAnim.stop() then a new roll from the CURRENT text with progress from 0, so a second replace cuts the first off and the intermediate texts are never seen rolling, contradicting the 2026-10-01 ruling that at 10 Hz the changing piece is seen rolling as it pans. A restart, not a queue. | 2026-10-13: W546 landed 2026-10-13: templates/marquee-main.qml queues a replace of an on-board item that arrives during a live roll in root.pendingReplaces (a LIST of queue entries, the same id merges, the latest text wins), exposes root.queuedRolls, and applies the next entry through replaceInPlace when the live roll stops (rollAnim.onStopped), from the text the board holds; swapRing clears the list (the swap rebuilds from the queue, which holds the latest text). replaceInPlace returns the shown-marked entries when everything was deferred, or the item would be owed a duplicate rotation. MEASURED before and after with the same burst (one arrival, five replace_visible of one id 100 ms apart, live widget, EL-Openglo, a 141-character item): before, no roll got past 0.12 and the intermediate texts were never seen; after, roll 1 runs 928 to 1328 ms (0 to 0.92) and roll 2 starts at once, 1360 to 1760 ms (0 to 0.96), the four later replaces merged into one entry (trace: apply pending left=0 inRing=true where=on). Two defects found by measuring and fixed: an id-keyed object (Object.keys returns the id as a string, the ring ids are numbers, so nothing matched; now a list) and an unverified claim that Qt drops an animation started from its own onStopped (a direct call works identically; the deferral and its comment were removed). qml_lint admitted 18, marquee_live admitted 0 deny 0 withheld, check_symbol 49 of 49, parity baseline for marquee-main.qml recorded, 18 stale screens re-rendered and byte-identical, action keys re-recorded, emitters checked. Not yet: samples do not carry queuedRolls (W548), and the roll speed does not follow the queue (W547).

waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-18: github-8f 2026-10-18: running monkeytype through uv --with in the scratch worktree is a repo-level tool choice, no operator ask (only a runtime dependency would be worth a note). Fleet rule: types from consumers, not casts or object. Traces give the types callers happen to pass, which can be broader than what the body needs, so judge each traced annotation against what the function does with it and keep the narrowest that satisfies the consumers. If it works, the home is an mtools pycodemod mode. | 2026-10-18: 2026-10-18: first trace ran check_urgency_cues.py as __main__, so monkeytype recorded only its helpers (cvd_gate, emitters, make_schemes, numpy...) and none of the target defs: a script must be traced as an imported module. Re-tracing through a scratch driver (importlib.import_module of check_urgency_cues, then _selftest()), a capped service; the repo forbids noqa, so the driver uses importlib and no late import. | 2026-10-18: 2026-10-18: monkeytype 23.3.0 cannot run its stub step on this repo: the project venv is Python 3.14.7 and monkeytype rewrite_Union and ReplaceTypedDictsWithStubs both fail on 3.14 Union internals (TypeError: member_descriptor object is not iterable), also with a no-op rewriter config. The trace itself works (21 traces recorded for check_urgency_cues once it is imported as a module, not run as __main__; decoding needs scripts on PYTHONPATH). Re-running the whole experiment under Python 3.13 in its own environment (UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT in the scratch dir, so the main venv is never touched). If it works, the mtools mode must pin the tracing interpreter below 3.14 or avoid monkeytype. | 2026-10-18: 2026-10-18 RESULT (monkeytype 23.3.0 under Python 3.13 in a scratch environment; the stub step fails on the project 3.14.7): trace of check_urgency_cues._selftest via an import driver, monkeytype stub then apply to the scratch worktree copy: scripts/check_urgency_cues.py house findings 965 -> 866 (-99, about 10 percent), repo total 36933 -> 36723. Traced types are broad: bare ndarray (house flags forbid bare generics), Dict[str, Union[...]] nested unions, so the Any survives; the fleet rule (types from consumers, narrowest that the body needs) needs TypedDict and NDArray forms the trace cannot produce. Verdict: trace-based annotation is a first pass worth about a tenth of a file, not a bulk lever. The selftest under the annotated file was not re-run (annotations only). | 2026-10-18: CORRECTION (github-8f 2026-10-18): do NOT pin the tracer below 3.14. The fleet floor is Python 3.14+ and a dependency without 3.14 support is the dependency problem. The mtools mode either uses a tracer fixed for 3.14 Union (patch monkeytype upstream, or a small tracer of our own on sys.monitoring) or skips tracing. The 3.13 environment here was only a way to take the measurement. The trace-then-narrow design is going to mtools as the pycodemod card.

Next: reproduce by writing with an untracked new spec present and again after git add; the observer sees TRACKED files only, so the untracked spec files being absent from its view is the first suspect, not the audit hook. | 2026-10-18: 2026-10-18 scratch worktree at 43ff327 (symlinked venv), one change at a time: (1) clean: write reads 506, 0 changed; (2) add an UNTRACKED root file: 506, 0 changed; (3) git add that root file: 507, 1 changed (it adds exactly itself). So the pytestspec closure DECLARES the root directory listing (every tracked root file, 99 of them the make_*.py family) in the 506 state; the 403 and 407 states are the ones where that listing was not declared (read as import-only by the audit hook). The question is therefore which run makes a non-import listing of the repo root and which does not, not whether tracked state matters. Candidate: a listing of the root for closures_*.bzl or policy leaves, done by opa_gate --specs itself (its closure presence check) or by pytest collection; the leaf count at the time (hypotheses or qml_target leaf present or absent) would flip it. | 2026-10-18: 2026-10-18 NAMED THE LISTING: running gate/stage.sh pytestspec in the scratch worktree under a variant of the observer hook that also logs the calling file, the repo root is listed by .venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/_pytest/pathlib.py (row 55 of the log, an R row, not importlib), then policy/ and policy/lib/ from the same file; scripts/opa_gate.py lists policy and policy/lib itself. So the 506 state is TRUE: pytest collection really lists the repo root, a genuine non-import read of the root names, and the closure rightly declares every root file. The 403 and 407 states are the anomaly: a run where that pytest listing did not happen, or happened and the hook did not see it. Unexplained which. | 2026-10-18: CORRECTION 2026-10-18 (operator): my last entry here concluded that the 506-file closure is the true one because pytest lists the repo root. That was wrong: it confuses content with structure. A listing reads the NAMES in a directory; declaring every root file as an input makes the stage sensitive to the bytes of all of them. The closure does not have to be flat: a listed directory is a structural dependency (its name set), a file opened is a content dependency, and the two are different kinds of input. Read this way the 403-file state was closer to right on content and lacked only the structural declaration; the 506 state over-declares content. The run-to-run flip is the same cause seen from the other side: when the hook logs an R listing of the root, every root file is declared as content; when it does not, none is and the names go undeclared.

residue.title: THE FIELD AS AN APERTURE INTEGRAL (operator 2026-09-22: pips with a brightness RANGE, modelled as a supersampled mask over a higher-resolution backdrop scrolled at the display rate — pinholes over a moving scene; the brain synthesizes the motion). Each pip's brightness = ghostAlpha + coverage * (1 - ghostAlpha), coverage = the backdrop's ink under the pip's aperture at the current offset. In QML: the backdrop (text, icon raster, sparkline, QR) drawn once into a ShaderEffectSource with mipmaps; a ShaderEffect over the static field samples per pip at an LOD matched to the aperture (the box integral for one lookup); the scroll offset is a uniform, so no Row rebuild ever happens. This is what a real LED sign's sub-pixel smooth scroll IS (PWM at fractional offsets). COLLAPSE candidate: W47 (viewport = the vertical uniform), W48 (a sparkline is a backdrop), W34(a) (lit dots ARE the field's, graded not snapped), and the live twin of segment_topology.project / matrix_glyph's offline coverage rule (ink under a cell aperture) — reuse-search hit, not a new operator

standing: Checks run under .venv/bin/python3; fix the tooling so it answers the question (no grep, sed or inline Python: a missing mode is work).

Pushes are automatic (post-commit auto_push, ff-only, logged in .git/auto-push.log); never push by hand or with --no-verify; wait for the marker `post-commit advisory (auto-captured)` in HEAD, and cite a sha only after it (land_template prints it).
No tree writes while check_tree_writes runs; commit through scripts/land_template.py (--commit, or --stack FILE), never git commit -a.
The worklist is the status: no open or closed field, WORKLIST.md is generated and never hand-edited, and no check may be unfalsifiable (--selftest, refuse unknown flags, report n of m).
A requirement is Rego (policy/NAME.rego plus NAME_test.rego, cases in policy/NAME.cases.json); the Python check only measures and emits --json.
Mutation-control each pytestspec port by renaming one rule id and confirming exactly the cases that expect it fail, then revert the rename without losing trailing spaces.
Queued stacks take turns in submit order (mtools W1463, pin 6877eaa or later), so a dependent stack may queue behind another; a repin or a closure-format change still lands alone with nothing queued.

Stage closures are observed with an import-listing audit hook (W666): a directory listing only the import system made declares nothing; run check_closure.py --holding FILE to see which closures hold a file.
